# Project ratings
**Practical estimates, 0–10—not measurements. Every project has numerical scores.**
Insight, depth and transfer refer to the strongest currently valuable contribution, not code volume. Inside value is reusable value distinct from the product; zero means no separately valuable contribution was identified in the supplied assessment.
Future value means total value **if the stated goal succeeds**, not probability-weighted value. Technical and delivery are ordinal plausibility judgements, not statistical forecasts. Confidence and short reasons are in the linked cards. No overall average is used.

<a id="agentic-animation"></a>
## agentic-animation
A local, project-agnostic pipeline for structured-story input, code-driven 2D puppet motion, replaceable media adapters, and narrated animation rendering.
The project is reported useful in current video-making and has three end-to-end demos, while its scope stops short of a stable product API or finished-film release. The estimates credit the working capability and reusable practices without assuming broader adoption or verification.
Assumption: Scores treat owner-reported use as credible evidence of current usefulness, not independent validation of every design claim.
- **deterministic-puppet-motion** — The deterministic motion constraints and explicit failure checks form a useful, reusable practice, though adapting them to other rigs would take work.
- **documented-story-pipeline** — The owner identifies a whole reusable authoring practice: story-script structure, word/action timing, async pre/post behavior and reusable assets prevent recurring coordination mistakes. This estimates that design insight and current owner reuse, not a claim of globally novel components or infallible code.
<a id="agentworld"></a>
## agentworld
An experimental event-driven civilization simulator with explicit actors, executable strategies, a cognitive call path, and recorded simulation interventions.
The workbench has useful allocation mechanisms and audit evidence, but its central equal-budget fidelity claim remains untested. If the intended research goal succeeds, it could provide a substantial capability for studying budgeted reasoning in simulations.
Assumption: Future value assumes the stated research goal succeeds and does not treat the unaccepted VS2 claim as established.
- **allocation-audit-record** — Recording allocation choices, budget and PRNG state in a hash-chained record before world commit is a thoughtful audit practice, though reuse requires adapting it to other transaction and scheduler designs.
<a id="aps"></a>
## aps
An experimental local planning workbench that models manufacturing item flows, compiles constraints, dispatches solver strategies, and presents schedules in a browser.
Current value is a prototype/workbench, not verified production scheduling. Conditional future value credits the owner-described ambition of a generalized cross-industry planning model with swappable engines, if that ambition succeeds; likelihood is scored separately.
Assumption: Future value refers to the owner-described universal APS ambition, not merely polishing the existing finite-schedule demo; current value still rates the actual prototype.
- **typed-item-flow-planning-model** — A typed model compiled to an immutable shared representation is a thoughtful basis for comparing methods, though reuse is bounded and solver semantic equivalence remains unverified.
<a id="auto-maintain-bench"></a>
## auto_maintain_bench
A benchmark for small language models diagnosing and maintaining Linux hosts through constrained bash interactions in isolated scenarios.
A useful focused research harness, but the owner finds even its best known agent outcome insufficiently useful for production. Current achieved value is modest; this does not diminish the transferable craft inside.
Assumption: Scores reflect the stated research-comparison scope, not production readiness or independently reproduced model performance.
- **safety-aware-scenario-scoring** — The owner places the specialized tiny-model trial craft above APS. The transferable value is the evaluation/reliability practice and safeguards, not merely having a scenario table or deployable agents; these are owner-calibrated estimates.
<a id="autofe"></a>
## autofe
An intent-driven frontend modeling engine that projects one semantic model into HTML, text, and Markdown renderings.
The gallery has practical value for its single owner, but remains an incomplete WIP with final acceptance pending. Its bounded scope and existing pipeline make completion plausible.
Assumption: Scores treat the prior reported gates as supporting feasibility, not as proof of final acceptance.
- **shared-target-neutral-renderer-decisions** — A useful, reusable boundary for keeping multiple renderers consistent, though its model and integration remain project-specific.
<a id="backseat"></a>
## backseat
A local-first desktop companion design with screen/system observation, hierarchical memory, a separate persona layer, and outlet plugins.
The design has useful structure and a concrete receipt safeguard, but the companion is partial and its real-world outcome and privacy behavior are unverified.
Assumption: Future value assumes the companion meets its stated goal for a single user.
- **honest-outlet-receipts** — Separating sent from confirmed-shown receipts is a thoughtful, reusable safeguard against overstating delivery.
<a id="beam"></a>
## beam
An archived hand-written beam-search decoder experiment layered on llama.cpp example infrastructure, focused on retaining candidate continuations through KV-cache sequence operations.
Its value is mainly as a historical reference for readers using the matching llama.cpp APIs; the archived, non-maintained state limits practical use. The implementation approach seems technically plausible, but the missing dependency snapshot and lack of a standalone build constrain delivery.
Assumption: Scores treat the stated historical-reference scope as the goal, rather than assuming a maintained current port.
- **llama-cpp-beam-decoder** — The decoder variants offer a narrow historical example of managing beam candidates with llama.cpp sequence operations, but depend on an unstable API snapshot and are not a standalone or transferable package.
<a id="causalmlp"></a>
## causalmlp
A synthetic-data experiment on prefix-visible hidden units in a single MLP, with a recorded report and result file; its evaluation comparison is under a documented metric-validity question.
The experiment has limited current value because its headline comparison is not valid evidence of an accuracy gap. If the scoped prefix-prediction goal succeeds, it could provide a useful, though bounded, result.
Assumption: Future value assumes the stated synthetic-data goal is completed with comparable metrics.
- **metric-comparability-finding** — The metric mismatch is a modest but broadly reusable evaluation warning that prevents invalid comparisons.
<a id="colleague-private"></a>
## colleague_private
A privacy-limited registered project; the existing sanitized record describes role-specific assistant skill directories and supporting knowledge assets, but content was not inspected.
The stated use is a narrow, private distillation for fun, with no identified broader product value; invoking a mature skill appears technically straightforward. No contribution cards were supplied.
Assumption: Assumes the supplied owner description accurately represents the project’s scope and intended use.
<a id="cuda"></a>
## cuda
A personal archive of hand-written CUDA tensor-core, attention, convolution, reduction, and sorting experiments with hardware-profiling notes.
The archive offers modest reference value to readers studying CUDA kernels, but per-file context, hardware requirements, and missing profiling outputs limit reuse. Its existing archive form is feasible to retain, though reproducing experiments is more demanding.
Assumption: Future value assumes the project remains a personal reference archive rather than becoming a maintained library.
<a id="cvorat"></a>
## cvorat
An unmaintained notebook lab of small byte-level language-model architecture experiments and shared custom layer code.
The notebooks offer a limited reference archive, but missing data and results make it hard to use or learn from today. Successful runs with documented results could make it a modestly useful experiment resource.
Assumption: Scores treat the stated exploratory training goal as worthwhile if completed and documented, without assuming novel findings.
- **shared-byte-lm-layers** — Shared layers could reduce duplication across experiments, but their correctness, results, and reuse beyond the archive are undocumented.
<a id="cz-bert"></a>
## cz_bert
A deprecated personal deep-learning sandbox containing old Transformer, data-kernel, nearest-neighbor, and CNN notebook experiments.
This is a modestly useful historical archive, but missing inputs, obsolete dependencies, and no current product audience limit practical value. Preserving it as an archaeological record appears feasible, though making the experiments runnable would be difficult.
Assumption: Future value assumes the goal is preservation and documentation, not restoring a modern runnable product.
<a id="cz-einn"></a>
## cz_einn
An archived one-person notebook research sketch expressing neural-network layers as Einstein-summation strings for character-level language-model experiments.
The archive preserves a modest architecture-prototyping idea, not working software or a demonstrated search capability. A successful realization could be a useful niche research tool, but delivery from this partial legacy notebook appears difficult.
Assumption: Future value assumes the stated string-based architecture search is made usable for research prototyping.
- **einsum-string-architecture-sketch** — A concrete, reusable way to specify layer variants as Einstein-index strings, though its narrow scope and lack of a captured result limit demonstrated value.
<a id="cz-noidea"></a>
## cz_noidea
A deprecated personal scratch archive of heterogeneous notebooks/scripts probing Python, asyncio, numerical libraries, neural networks, and throughput.
This is a preserved personal scratch archive, not a coherent product; its disconnected experiments and missing inputs constrain practical use. A modestly more navigable reference archive seems technically achievable, but no specific future goal or audience is established.
Assumption: Future value assumes the archive is made easier to browse without turning it into a maintained library or application.
<a id="cznn"></a>
## cznn
A compositional PyTorch layer library for building neural-network variants from sequential, residual, parallel, and parameter-counting primitives.
Repeated owner reuse and documented core tests support meaningful value as a personal research tool; lack of packaging and maintenance limits broader product value.
Assumption: Scores assume the intended audience remains the owner and adjacent researchers running small PyTorch experiments.
- **point-free-layer-composition** — A compact composition algebra plus parameter counting makes small-model comparisons easier to express and reuse, though it is a practical research pattern rather than a novel modeling advance.
<a id="danmaku"></a>
## danmaku
A small PyQt5/X11 scrolling-comment overlay with a one-shot demo, a push-driven engine, and a storm-model experiment.
A complete, focused X11 utility has plausible practical value for its narrow audience; limited verification and platform requirements constrain broader value.
Assumption: Scores treat the documented engine and delivery form as substantially representative, without assuming measured performance.
- **single-raster-per-comment-overlay** — Rasterizing each comment once and moving its own surface is a useful, reusable rendering choice, though its performance benefit is unmeasured and reuse is constrained by X11.
<a id="dino-py"></a>
## dino.py
Experimental DINOv2/DINOv3 feature extraction through a hand-built ggml graph, plus smart-crop and video keyframe/crop scripts.
The scripts offer useful local feature-extraction and crop workflows, but hard-coded model paths, external assets, and limited packaging narrow their practical reach. The forward path appears technically plausible, though it was inspected rather than run.
Assumption: Scores treat the scripts as useful to technically capable users who can supply matching model assets and dependencies.
- **ggml-dino-forward-path** — Building a ggml graph for DINO’s patch embeddings and transformer layers is a meaningful implementation effort, but reuse is constrained by local GGUF weights and ggml bindings.
<a id="dinoseg"></a>
## dinoseg
An archived OpenCV GUI for click-labeled image masks using frozen DINOv3 patch features with kNN and linear-probe predictions.
This is a modest research aid rather than a usable segmentation product today; completing a useful low-label workflow seems technically plausible but requires substantial packaging and validation.
Assumption: Future value assumes the intended exploration becomes a usable, validated low-label segmentation workflow.
- **frozen-feature-mask-gui** — A practical exploratory combination of frozen DINOv3 features, click labels, and kNN/linear-probe masks, but its narrow GUI has no validation or export path.
<a id="disk"></a>
## disk
A personal archive mixing unreproducible thermal-control/machine-vision experiments with industrial-camera and object-storage helpers; the source status says it never became a project.
As an incomplete personal archive without a current audience or supported project goal, its present practical value is limited; a validated solver reference could add modest value.
Assumption: Scores assume the stated archive-reference scope and do not treat the notebook as scientifically validated.
- **analytic-diffusion-reference** — The analytic reference is a potentially useful, nontrivial check for a narrow PDE class, but its equations and output remain unvalidated.
<a id="dojo"></a>
## dojo
A local CLI and SQLite proof of concept for storing revisable, sourced discussion candidates, alternatives, objections, unknowns and relations; its intended network-level product is not implemented.
The local CLI/store is a useful, narrow demonstration, while the broader network-level product could offer substantial value if it preserves disagreement and privacy in real discussions. The stated direction is technically plausible but remains materially beyond the implemented local proof of concept.
Assumption: Future value assumes a usable network-level product that connects discussions without certifying truth or exposing private discussion.
- **dojo-claim-lifecycle** — The inspectable lifecycle carefully preserves provenance, revisions, disagreement and uncertainty without conflating confirmation with truth; it is a useful bounded pattern, though structured argument is an established category and reuse requires adaptation.
<a id="drive"></a>
## drive
A closed offline browser driving simulator using a checked-in Suzhou OSM extract, lane-aware navigation, traffic, weather, collisions, hazards and roadside decoration.
A completed, bounded offline driving demo offers practical value to a niche audience, but the packet establishes no differentiated user benefit over a close comparator. Its reported build and tests support strong feasibility estimates for the stated one-city scope.
Assumption: Treat the reported completion status as representative of the pinned project state.
- **drive-lane-routing-module** — It combines directional routing, lane-transition restrictions and maneuver guidance into a useful route module, but remains coupled to the app and map representation.
<a id="expyssion"></a>
## expyssion
A Python-hosted expression language with a frozen v1 specification and interpreter; expressions and calls are the central design, with control structures represented as functions of callables.
A complete, inspectable experimental language is useful to language-design learners, but its intentionally narrow scope limits broader product value. The stated closed-v1 goal is already delivered.
Assumption: Scores treat the frozen specification and working Python-hosted interpreter as the intended finished product.
- **expyssion-syncpoint-semantics** — The explicit sync-point effect model and distinct assigned-versus-consumed callable behavior form a thoughtful, reusable semantics design, though its transfer is bounded and implementation reuse is costly.
<a id="fat-kakeya-needle"></a>
## fat_kakeya_needle
A mathematical and computational research workbench on minimizing the swept area of a 1×ε rectangle during a continuous half-turn with unrestricted planar motion.
The workbench combines a potentially significant reported asymptotic result with careful limits on what its numerical candidates establish. Its value would rise substantially if the proof withstands mathematical review.
Assumption: Scores treat the documented theorem as a credible research result, not as independently verified.
- **fat-continuous-motion-bridge** — The reported bridge between a Kakeya neighborhood bound and unrestricted continuous needle motion is a substantial, non-obvious proof strategy, though its scope is specialized and independent acceptance remains open.
<a id="flashdb"></a>
## flashdb
An experimental single-node Rust document-store substrate and workload-driven physical-layout research project; current documents conflict about whether adaptation behavior is implemented and what measurements support it.
The prototype offers modest present value as a bounded research substrate; successful workload-learned layout could make it substantially more useful to database researchers. Conflicting implementation claims and unverified results temper delivery and feasibility estimates.
Assumption: Future value assumes the stated bounded single-node learned-layout research goal succeeds, not a general production database.
- **flashdb-storage-substrate** — A real, tested-in-source WAL/memtable/tile substrate and focused order-flow adapter provide a useful research foundation, but the integration is narrow and not a general learned-layout engine.
<a id="fring"></a>
## fring
An archive of Python/Linux io_uring experiments comparing raw ring loops, an asyncio/uvloop bridge and a hand-written coroutine scheduler on server/client examples.
As a learning archive, fring offers some value for studying io_uring and event-loop layers, but does not establish a useful performance result or transferable practice. Its stated script-based scope is plausible to deliver, though the scheduler is not verified as a reusable library.
Assumption: Scores treat fring as an archival learning resource, not as a maintained or performance-validated event-loop library.
- **fring-zring-module** — The custom scheduler offers a modest source-study example of event-loop components, but implicit lifecycle and compatibility details limit reuse.
<a id="grammar"></a>
## grammar
A notebook research archive asking whether a convolutional U-Net encoder-decoder can reconstruct masked Python source tokens without recurrence or attention.
The archive has limited present research utility, while a completed comparison could be useful within its narrow question. The approach is technically plausible, but missing data and CUDA-dependent notebooks make delivery less certain.
Assumption: Future value assumes the corpus is restored and the architectures are evaluated reproducibly.
- **grammar-notebook-experiment** — The U-Net approach is a modestly non-obvious experiment, but missing data and evaluation limit what the notebooks and logs establish; a reproducible comparison could offer narrow research value.
<a id="helpagent"></a>
## helpagent
A completed research campaign and harness measuring a fixed small local model in bounded plan/implement/verify/claim workflows against a mature agent CLI and blind external grader; the proposed user-facing repository-fixing command does not exist.
The completed campaign has useful bounded research and negative-result value, not a shipped repository-fixing product. Its strongest reusable asset is trustworthy claim evaluation rather than the tested model's production capability.
Assumption: Parent estimate from the existing packet after the scoring child received a provider API 499; no extra investigation or experiment was run.
- **helpagent-blind-claim-evidence-practice** — A blind external grader, pristine-copy evaluation, canary and enforced claim gate form a thoughtful transferable evaluation practice, even though the particular agent campaign did not establish general superiority.
<a id="hfget"></a>
## hfget
A closed one-file Python helper that searches Hugging Face model repositories, ranks GGUF candidates and shards, selects companion files and downloads the chosen set.
A complete, single-file helper could save effort for its intended personal workflow, though its selection behavior and advantage over existing options are unverified. Its limited scope makes implementation plausible, with API behavior and large downloads adding delivery risk.
Assumption: The selection preferences match the user's needs and the helper works with current Hub behavior.
- **hfget-selector-tool** — Combining preference-based GGUF ranking, shard grouping, and companion selection is a useful but narrow workflow policy whose reuse is limited by configuration and Hub/API upkeep.
<a id="horse-video"></a>
## horse_video
A closed code-authored 15-second horse-running animation using Remotion, SVG and Three.js primitives, seeded scenery and a local soundtrack; the README presents it as a single art experiment, not an animation framework.
The owner regards this finite video as a trivial output rather than a useful project or reusable creation capability. This is his catalogue-value judgement, not a claim that all artwork lacks value.
Assumption: Treat the reported render as a completed artifact, but do not assume unreviewed visual quality.
- **horse-video-render** — The owner identifies no significant reusable practice here: it is one finite video using existing tools, unlike the reusable animation system. The score estimates contribution value, not the unseen film's artistic quality.
<a id="http-mock"></a>
## http_mock
An archived notebook experiment generating synthetic toy protocol traces and training a character-level GRU encoder-decoder to imitate mock-server responses, including cycle losses and a request/response grid variant.
As archived, this is an unevaluated research attempt rather than a usable mock server or demonstrated model. If completed, it could provide a modest toy demonstration of learned stateful-protocol imitation, though notebook and evaluation gaps constrain delivery.
Assumption: Future value assumes the toy protocol can be learned and demonstrated with a reproducible evaluation.
- **http-mock-notebook-output** — The GRU and cross-grid variants suggest a modest exploratory angle, but no preserved results establish a reusable method or learned behavior.
<a id="huaqiang-game"></a>
## huaqiang_game
A paused game-design lab for a social-stealth encounter, with a Python rules prototype, browser greybox and Godot vertical slice in a fictional industrial city.
The existing prototypes offer a useful but unvalidated encounter experiment; a successful compact slice could become a worthwhile playable experience. The paused status lowers delivery feasibility despite a technically plausible, bounded goal.
Assumption: Future value assumes the goal remains a single encounter rather than the conditional 6–8 hour game.
- **huaqiang-game-prototype-output** — The encounter models distinct social and witness-driven consequences, but its value and reuse remain limited without player evaluation or a transferable design package.
<a id="huaqiang-video"></a>
## huaqiang_video
A closed Remotion composition that encodes the Huaqiang melon story beats and timing in source and reports a 70-second audiovisual render.
The owner regards this finite video as a trivial output rather than a useful project or reusable creation capability. This is his catalogue-value judgement, not a claim that all artwork lacks value.
Assumption: Scores treat the reported render as an available prototype, not as independently reviewed media.
- **huaqiang-video-render** — The owner identifies no significant reusable practice here: it is one finite video using existing tools, unlike the reusable animation system. The score estimates contribution value, not the unseen film's artistic quality.
<a id="hyperframaker"></a>
## hyperframaker
A local-first browser canvas for connecting, generating, inspecting and regenerating artifact nodes through a filesystem-backed registry, manifests and agent scripts.
The local canvas is a concrete and potentially enjoyable creator tool; a reliable inspect-and-regenerate workflow would have more value than the current experimental app. Its underlying thought is below the owner's APS example rather than a new paradigm.
Assumption: Parent estimate from the supplied packet and owner feedback after the scoring child's provider API 499; no live generation was run.
- **hyperframaker-local-graph-output** — The multimodal file/script/manifest canvas is a useful composition of established graph practices, but not a large conceptual departure from ComfyUI or Node-RED.
<a id="ideas"></a>
## ideas
A closed archive of speculative notes about learning systems, attention/memory, time-series forecasting and programming languages; the README labels them hypotheses rather than validated papers or production designs.
This is a complete, low-cost ideation archive with modest present utility and potential to guide a bounded experiment. It is not evidence of an established research finding.
Assumption: Future value assumes a researcher selects a claim and develops a discriminating experiment.
- **ideas-speculative-notes** — The notes offer a compact starting point for framing experiments, but their central claims are explicitly unvalidated and require substantial follow-up.
<a id="jpi-fe"></a>
## jpi.fe
An unfinished Vue 3 front end for editing nested JSON as recursive tables, designed to call a separately hosted paginated REST API that is not included.
